subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Should the five-minute base plus 256 KiB/s transfer budget become the Microsoft Teams fail-closed policy, with this PR landing before the overlapping SharePoint timeout PR?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but selecting a deadline that can fail existing very slow uploads and deciding which branch owns the shared helper are compatibility and delivery choices requiring Microsoft Teams owner intent.

options.title: Approve and land this first
options.body: Accept the transfer-aware deadline, merge this narrower file-consent change, and rebase the related SharePoint PR to reuse the merged helper.

options.title: Coordinate one combined landing
options.body: Pause both PRs until a single branch reconciles the shared helper and proves both consent and SharePoint upload paths.

options.title: Reject fail-closed uploads
options.body: Decline the timeout policy if Microsoft Teams uploads should remain unbounded rather than surface an error after a conservative deadline.

recommendation.title: Approve and land this first
recommendation.body: Accept the transfer-aware deadline, merge this narrower file-consent change, and rebase the related SharePoint PR to reuse the merged helper.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available Microsoft Teams-specific routing candidate from the current repository context, although direct file-history attribution remains incomplete.
